When you pour a spoonful of instant coffee into hot milk, you expect a smooth cup that tastes just like the cafe favorite you order on a weekend. Yet, many Indian households report a subtle texture shift that appears after the first sip. This phenomenon is not a mystery of the water or the milk; it is a direct result of the ingredient ratios inside the jar itself.

**Understanding the ingredient panel**

Instant coffee manufacturers in India often blend coffee with chicory, a roasted root that adds bulk and a distinct flavor. While chicory can be pleasant in certain traditional mixes, it behaves differently when combined with milk proteins. Chicory particles tend to bind loosely, creating a slightly distinct mouthfeel that becomes noticeable once the initial coffee-water solution stabilises. This is why the first sip feels fine – the coffee dissolves quickly – but subsequent sips reveal the proportion of the blend.

**Why transparency matters**

Purity Beans took a clear step by making the exact coffee-to-chicory ratio visible on the back of every Ultra Blend jar. The label reads a clear 70% coffee, 30% chicory formulation. No vague terms, no hidden percentages. This transparency empowers you to make an informed choice. Knowing the ratio lets you predict how the coffee will interact with milk, water, or any other base you prefer in your daily routine.

**Everyday brewing economics**

When evaluating a pantry staple, cost per cup remains a vital metric for home brewers. Purity Beans Ultra Blend is priced at ₹309 for a 100g glass jar. Because the packaging provides at least 66 servings per container, the math brings the cost down to about ₹5 a cup. This makes it an accessible choice for households that enjoy a daily milk coffee without inflating their monthly grocery budget.

**The role of seventy thirty blends**

Many coffee drinkers transition from commercial chicory mixtures to a balanced blend. Having 30% chicory in Ultra Blend softens the overall profile, making it pair exceptionally well with dairy.
